title: Diagnostic accuracy of smartphone-based tele dentistry: Individual- and tooth-level findings from a community study
content:
by Syeda Kanza Naqvi, Yasir Ali, Meena Rathi, Zahid Ali, Muhammad Sajid, Shayan Imran, Arjumand Rizvi, Zahra Ali Padhani, Salima Alibhai, Jai K. Das

Tele-dentistry offers a potential alternative to improve access to oral health services. Unlike previous approaches, our study evaluates tele-dentistry in real-life conditions with a detailed tooth-level analysis, addressing gaps in granular diagnostic approaches. The study used purposive sampling to identify participants aged five to 20 years from Karachi. Clinical examinations to check for visible cavitations without radiographs were conducted to determine the caries index using DMFT index. Photographs were taken from five angles, coded, and reviewed by a second dentist for analysis. We calculated Kappa, sensitivity, specificity, negative predictive values, and positive predictive values at individual and tooth level. The study included 600 children and the Kappa co-efficient between tele dentistry and physical examination for the individual level and tooth level diagnosis were 0.624 and 0.426 respectively. The sensitivity in individual and tooth level analysis was 87.9%(CI:84.2%;91.1%) and 50.3%(CI:47.6%;53.1%) and specificity was 73.6%(CI:67.5%;79.1%) and 94.2%(CI:93.8%;94.6%) respectively. The sensitivity for caries diagnosis through tele-dentistry in primary teeth was lower (47.8%;CI:44.5%,51.1%) compared to the permanent teeth (56%;CI:51%;60.8%) at tooth level, while opposite trend was observed at the individual level. These findings indicate higher reliability for identifying individuals with caries than for detecting specific affected teeth and underscore the need for assessing more rigorous diagnostic methodologies including the use of artificial intelligence. Improving image quality and standardizing training for image capture and assessment may enhance diagnostic accuracy and support the effective use of tele-dentistry in real-world settings.
